tzatziki.name: Roasted Red Pepper Cream Sauce
tzatziki.note: This is Monday’s pepper-cream sauce for two. The grocery list includes it with the dinner.
tzatziki.macrosNote: Nutrition is for the full combined sauce batch.

ingredients.item: Roasted red peppers (jarred) — 115 g
Heavy cream — 125 g
Butter — 1.75 tbsp

steps: Drain and blot the roasted peppers, then blend with the cream until smooth.

Pour into the chicken skillet and simmer uncovered until the sauce coats a spoon. Use the portion of the measured butter remaining after roasting the beans and searing the chicken to finish the sauce.

dinners.name: Smoky Paprika Chicken Thighs + Green Beans with Roasted-Red-Pepper Cream
dinners.note: Roast the beans while the chicken sears. Reduce the pepper cream uncovered so it coats the thighs.

ingredients.item: Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless) — Jake 285 g raw, Laine 230 g raw
Green beans — Jake 130 g, Laine 110 g
Roasted red peppers (jarred) — Jake 65 g, Laine 50 g
Heavy cream — Jake 70 g, Laine 55 g
Butter — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine 0.75 tbsp
Smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt — Jake 0.5 tsp, Laine 0.5 tsp

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Dry the green beans, toss with about one-third of the butter, melted, and a pinch of salt. Roast in one layer for 15–20 minutes, turning once.

Pat the thighs dry and season with the spice mix, using smoked paprika as the main flavor. Sear in a skillet with a little of the remaining butter over medium-high heat until both sides are golden. Lower the heat as needed and cook the thickest piece to 165°F. Transfer the chicken to a plate.

Drain and blot the jarred peppers, then blend with the cream. Pour into the chicken skillet and simmer uncovered, stirring, until the sauce coats a spoon. Stir in the remaining butter, return the chicken to coat, and serve with the beans.

photo.alt: Smoky Paprika Chicken Thighs + Green Beans with Roasted-Red-Pepper Cream

dinners.name: Crispy Pulled-Pork Carnitas Lettuce Cups + Lime-Cabbage Slaw + Avocado Crema
dinners.note: Start with 1 kg boneless pork shoulder for both dinners. The Ingredients list shows Tuesday’s allocations. Saturday uses 365 g of cooked pork from this batch.

ingredients.item: Pork shoulder (raw) — Jake 225 g raw, Laine 180 g raw
Romaine lettuce — Jake 75 g, Laine 60 g
Green cabbage — Jake 75 g, Laine 60 g
Avocado — Jake 0.375 avocado, Laine 0.25 avocado
Daisy sour cream — Jake 2 tbsp, Laine 1.5 tbsp
Lime juice — Jake 0.75 tbsp, Laine 0.5 tbsp
Yellow onion — Jake 0.125 cup, Laine 0.125 cup
Smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt — Jake 0.75 tsp, Laine 0.5 tsp

steps: Weigh 405 g raw boneless pork shoulder for Tuesday and 595 g for Saturday. Keep the two cuts identifiable in the slow cooker. Soften the minced onion in a skillet first, then add it with the spices, a pinch of salt and a splash of water. Cook on LOW until fork-tender, about 7–9 hours. Check the smaller cut first.

Shred the Saturday cut separately and set aside 365 g cooked for the stuffed peppers. If that cut yields less, freeze what it yields and portion Saturday’s filling in roughly a 205:160 ratio. Freeze the reserved pork flat in a shallow container within 2 hours and move it to the refrigerator Friday night to thaw.
Shred the Tuesday cut, divide it in a 225:180 ratio by cooked weight and crisp the portions in a hot skillet or under the broiler. Spoon off any excess pooled fat before crisping.

Toss finely shredded cabbage with most of the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Mash avocado with sour cream and the rest of the lime. Pat the romaine dry and fill the leaves with the pork, slaw and crema.

photo.alt: Crispy pork carnitas in lettuce cups with cabbage slaw and avocado crema

dinners.name: Turkey Meatballs in Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Sauce + Zucchini Ribbons
dinners.note: The ribbons cook in about a minute. Keep them separate from the sauce until plating.

ingredients.item: Ground turkey 93/7 — Jake 245 g raw, Laine 190 g raw
Sun-dried tomatoes (dry) — Jake 9 g, Laine 8 g
Heavy cream — Jake 65 g, Laine 55 g
Parmesan cheese (grated) — Jake 3 tbsp, Laine 2.5 tbsp
Zucchini — Jake 125 g, Laine 130 g
Olive oil — Jake 0.5 tbsp, Laine 0.375 tbsp
Garlic — Jake 1 clove, Laine 1 clove

steps: Mix the turkey with half the Parmesan, the minced garlic, salt and pepper. Form small meatballs, keeping the Jake and Laine batches separate so each gets their measured portion.
Heat the measured olive oil in a skillet. Brown the meatballs on two sides, then lower the heat and cook through to 165°F. Transfer to a plate.

Finely chop the dry sun-dried tomatoes. Add to the skillet with the cream, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer uncovered until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Return the meatballs to the sauce.
Use a vegetable peeler to make zucchini ribbons. Pat dry and sauté in a hot skillet for 1–2 minutes, just until flexible. Top with the sauced meatballs and the remaining Parmesan.

photo.alt: Turkey Meatballs in Creamy Sun-Dried Tomato Sauce + Zucchini Ribbons

dinners.name: THANKSGIVING: Filet Mignon + Lobster Tails, Brown-Butter Cauliflower Mash, Garlic-Butter Mushrooms, Asparagus + Chocolate Espresso Mousse
dinners.note: Holiday dinner for two. The macros include chocolate espresso mousse.

ingredients.item: Filet mignon (raw) — Jake 220 g, Laine 180 g
Lobster tail meat (raw) — Jake 150 g, Laine 120 g
Cauliflower — Jake 220 g, Laine 170 g
Cremini mushrooms — Jake 180 g, Laine 150 g
Asparagus — Jake 160 g, Laine 130 g
Butter — Jake 3.1 tbsp, Laine 2.6 tbsp
Cream cheese — Jake 2.333 tbsp, Laine 1.667 tbsp
Parmesan cheese (grated) — Jake 3.6 tbsp, Laine 2.8 tbsp
Heavy cream — Jake 80 g, Laine 65 g
Dark chocolate 85% — Jake 25 g, Laine 20 g
Coffee espresso brewed — Jake 20 g, Laine 15 g
Sugar-free sweetener (monk fruit) — Jake 4 g, Laine 3 g
Garlic — Jake 2 clove, Laine 1.5 clove

photo.alt: THANKSGIVING: Filet Mignon + Lobster Tails, Brown-Butter Cauliflower Mash, Garlic-Butter Mushrooms, Asparagus + Chocolate Espresso Mousse

stepSections.title: Filet mignon
steps: Pat the filets dry and season both sides with salt and pepper. Keep the 220 g filet for Jake and the 180 g filet for Laine.

Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the filets for about 2–3 minutes per side, then briefly sear the edges. Reduce the heat, add a portion of the measured butter, and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks as they finish.
Check each filet in the center with an instant-read thermometer. Remove each when it reaches 145°F and rest for at least 3 minutes before serving. The smaller filet may finish first.

stepSections.title: Butter-broiled lobster tails
steps: Thaw frozen tails in the refrigerator. With kitchen shears, split each top shell lengthwise, stopping at the tail fan. Loosen the meat and lift it over the shell, leaving it attached at the base.
Preheat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below the element. Set the tails on a broiler-safe pan and brush the exposed meat with melted butter.
Broil until pearly and opaque throughout and the thickest part reaches 145°F. Start checking at 5 minutes and remove each tail as it finishes.

stepSections.title: Garlic-butter pressure-cooked mushrooms
steps: Clean and trim 330 g whole cremini mushrooms. Mince the 3½ cloves of garlic. Put the mushrooms, garlic and a portion of the measured butter in the cooker.
Add water or broth according to the minimum liquid requirement for your cooker. Cook at high pressure for 2 minutes, then quick-release according to the cooker instructions.

With the lid off, use sauté mode to reduce the cooking liquid. If the cooker required extra liquid, spoon some out first. Toss until the mushrooms are glossy and coated. Divide between Jake and Laine using their 180 g and 150 g raw allocations.

stepSections.title: Roasted asparagus
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Trim the tough ends and pat the spears dry. Toss with a little of the measured melted butter, salt and pepper.
Spread in a single layer and roast for 8–12 minutes, checking thin spears first. Pull the pan when the asparagus is bright green and tender-crisp, before switching the oven to broil for the lobster.

stepSections.title: Brown-butter cauliflower mash
steps: Cut 390 g cauliflower into even florets. Steam until very soft, about 12–15 minutes. Drain well and let the excess moisture steam off.
Mash or blend the hot cauliflower with the cream cheese and Parmesan until smooth. Taste and season.
Cook a portion of the measured butter over medium heat, swirling until the milk solids are golden and smell nutty. Take it off the heat immediately and stir it into the mash. Cover and keep warm.

stepSections.title: Chocolate espresso mousse
steps: Make the mousse a few hours ahead. Chop 45 g dark chocolate, melt gently and let it cool until just warm. Brew 35 g espresso and let it cool.
Whip 145 g cold heavy cream with 7 g monk fruit sweetener to soft peaks. Stir the espresso into the chocolate, then whisk in a spoonful of whipped cream to lighten it.
Gently fold the chocolate mixture into the remaining whipped cream. Divide between two ramekins and chill until set, about 2 hours.

stepSections.title: Cooking timeline
steps: At least 2 hours before dinner, make and refrigerate the mousse. Prep the vegetables and lobster tails, then refrigerate the tails until ready to broil.
About 40 minutes before serving, preheat the oven to 425°F and get the cauliflower steaming and the pressure cooker heating. Finish the mash and reduce the mushroom sauce while the other dishes cook.
About 15 minutes before serving, put the asparagus in the oven and begin searing the filets. Check both filets separately and let them rest once they reach temperature.
Pull the asparagus and switch to broil. Cook the lobster while the filets rest, then plate with the warm mash, mushrooms and asparagus. Serve the chilled mousse after dinner.

dinners.name: Sesame-Ginger Salmon + Crispy Bok Choy + Cucumber-Sesame Salad
dinners.note: Use freezer salmon if available. Thaw it in the refrigerator the night before.

ingredients.item: Atlantic salmon (raw) — Jake 250 g raw, Laine 200 g raw
Bok choy — Jake 165 g, Laine 140 g
English cucumber — Jake 120 g, Laine 100 g
Sesame oil — Jake 0.75 tbsp, Laine 0.75 tbsp
Sesame seeds — Jake 1.5 tbsp, Laine 1 tbsp
Soy sauce (reduced sodium) — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine 0.75 tbsp
Fresh ginger — Jake 8 g, Laine 6 g
Rice vinegar — Jake 0.75 tbsp, Laine 0.75 tbsp

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Dry the salmon. Mix the soy sauce, grated ginger and half the sesame oil, brush on the salmon, and roast until the thickest part of each fillet reaches 145°F. Start checking around 10 minutes.

Halve the bok choy, rinse between the leaves and dry well. Use the remaining oil to sear it cut-side down in a hot skillet until browned. Add a small splash of water and cover briefly to tenderize the stems, then uncover to evaporate excess water.
Slice the cucumbers and pat dry if wet. Toss with rice vinegar and sesame seeds just before serving.

photo.alt: Sesame-Ginger Salmon + Crispy Bok Choy + Cucumber-Sesame Salad

dinners.name: Pulled-Pork Stuffed Peppers + Cheddar, Sour Cream & Crunchy Cabbage
dinners.note: Use Tuesday’s reserved cooked pork. One large bell pepper half per person works well.

ingredients.item: Reserved pulled pork — Jake 205 g cooked, Laine 160 g cooked
Bell pepper — Jake 115 g, Laine 100 g
Cheddar cheese — Jake 35 g, Laine 30 g
Daisy sour cream — Jake 2 tbsp, Laine 1.5 tbsp
Green cabbage — Jake 45 g, Laine 45 g
Lime juice — Jake 0.75 tbsp, Laine 0.5 tbsp

steps: Thaw the portion of pork frozen on Tuesday in the refrigerator overnight. Heat the oven to 400°F. Halve and seed the peppers and roast cut-side up for about 12 minutes.

Tip out any water from the peppers. Fill Jake’s half with about 205 g cooked pork and Laine’s with about 160 g. Add each portion’s cheddar, using any filling that does not fit alongside. Bake until the filling reaches 165°F in the center, about 12–18 minutes.
Toss the shredded cabbage with lime and a pinch of salt just before serving. Spoon the sour cream over the hot peppers.

photo.alt: Pulled-Pork Stuffed Peppers + Cheddar, Sour Cream & Crunchy Cabbage

dinners.name: Chicken Thigh Piccata-Style Skillet + Butter-Cream Caper Sauce + Roasted Cauliflower
dinners.note: Use the browned bits in the chicken skillet to flavor the lemon-caper cream sauce.

ingredients.item: Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless) — Jake 285 g raw, Laine 225 g raw
Cauliflower — Jake 175 g, Laine 150 g
Heavy cream — Jake 60 g, Laine 50 g
Butter — Jake 0.875 tbsp, Laine 0.625 tbsp
Capers — Jake 1 tbsp, Laine 0.75 tbsp
Lemon juice — Jake 0.75 tbsp, Laine 0.5 tbsp
Parmesan cheese (grated) — Jake 2.5 tbsp, Laine 2 tbsp

steps: Dry the cauliflower florets and spread them on a parchment-lined pan in one layer. Toss with some of the melted butter and roast at 425°F until browned at the edges, about 25 minutes.

Pat the thighs dry and season. Sear in a heavy skillet with a little of the remaining butter until browned. Lower the heat and continue until the thickest piece reaches 165°F, then transfer to a plate.
Drain the capers. Deglaze the skillet with the lemon juice and a small splash of water, scraping up the browned bits. Lower the heat, add cream and capers, and simmer gently until spoon-coating.
Take off the heat and stir in the remaining butter and Parmesan. Return the chicken to coat and serve with the roasted cauliflower.

photo.alt: Chicken Thigh Piccata-Style Skillet + Butter-Cream Caper Sauce + Roasted Cauliflower

jakeLunch.name: Creamy Chipotle-Style Chicken Thighs, Bell Peppers, Cheddar & Broccoli
jakeLunch.note: Prep on Sunday for Monday–Wednesday. The ingredient amounts are for three containers. The nutrition shown is per container.

ingredients.item: Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless) — 825 g raw
Bell pepper — 150 g
Broccoli florets — 150 g
Heavy cream — 150 g
Cream cheese — 4.5 tbsp
Cheddar cheese — 90 g
Hatch diced green chiles — 45 g
Smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt — 2.25 tsp

steps: Season the chicken with the smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt. Sear in batches if needed so the thighs brown. Set the chicken aside.

Soften the sliced bell pepper in the skillet. Add the heavy cream, cream cheese and drained Hatch chiles. Stir over medium-low until smooth, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken and simmer gently to 165°F. Reduce uncovered until thick enough to coat the chicken.
Steam the broccoli just until crisp-tender and drain well. Take the chicken off the heat and stir in the cheddar. Divide the chicken, peppers, sauce and broccoli evenly into 3 containers.
Refrigerate the containers within 2 hours in a fridge at 40°F or below. Reheat each portion to 165°F, stirring the sauce halfway through.

photo.alt: Creamy chicken thighs with peppers, cheddar and broccoli in a glass meal prep container

weekendMeals.name: Bacon, Avocado & Cheddar Omelet + Cucumber Salad

ingredients.item: Eggs (large) — 3 eggs
Bacon — 100 g raw
Avocado — 0.5 avocado
Cheddar cheese — 40 g
English cucumber — 125 g

steps: Weigh the bacon raw, then fry until crisp. Drain it and wipe the skillet so the rendered bacon fat stays separate. Dice or crumble the bacon.
Whisk the eggs and pour them into a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. When nearly set, add the bacon and shredded cheddar. Fold and cook until the eggs are set and the center reaches 160°F.
Serve with the sliced avocado and cold cucumber.

photo.alt: Bacon and cheddar omelet with sliced avocado and cucumber salad

weekendMeals.name: Thick Creamy Roasted Poblano, Chicken, Cheddar & Bacon Soup
weekendMeals.note: Saturday’s ingredient amounts make one six-portion pot: three Jake portions and three Laine portions. Split the finished soup by weight in a 5:4 ratio for Jake and Laine, then divide each share into three. Serve one each, refrigerate one each for Sunday and keep the extra pair.

ingredients.item: Chicken thighs (boneless, skinless) — 1080 g raw for the pot
Poblano pepper — 351 g for the pot
Bacon — 324 g raw for the pot
Cheddar cheese — 135 g for the pot
Cream cheese — 157 g for the pot
Heavy cream — 243 g for the pot
Chicken broth — 540 g for the pot
Yellow onion — 0.54 cup for the pot
Garlic — 6.75 cloves for the pot

steps: Broil the poblanos, turning until blistered all over. Cover for 10 minutes, then peel, seed and dice. Cook the minced onion until fully soft and stir in the garlic for the last 30 seconds.

Weigh the bacon raw, cook it until crisp, and drain. After the poblanos come out, set the oven to 425°F. Spread the thighs on a separate rimmed tray and roast to 165°F, about 20–25 minutes. Shred the chicken. Hold back some bacon for topping, dividing the topping between the portions in the same 5:4 ratio.
Add roasted poblano, broth and softened cream cheese to the onion. Blend part of the base if you prefer it smoother, then stir in the heavy cream and simmer gently, uncovered, until spoon-coating.

Take the pot off the heat. Stir in the freshly shredded cheddar a handful at a time, then fold in the shredded chicken and most of the bacon. Stir well before weighing and dividing the soup. Top with the reserved bacon.
Refrigerate the remaining portions in shallow containers within 2 hours. Label one Jake and one Laine portion for Sunday.

photo.alt: Thick creamy poblano chicken cheddar and bacon soup
